author: ohtadmin
title: Firm hired to help design Getty
text:
The town council has approved $52,990 to hire a design consultant to assist with the planning of Fort Getty in cooperation with the park’s ad hoc committee.
The councilors awarded the contract to Beta Group at their Nov. 3 meeting. Jamestown resident Arek Galle, who helped develop the master plan for Beavertail State Park, will manage the project for the firm.
Randall Collins, vice president of Beta, pitched his firm in a letter dated July 15.
“Beta has been a part of several projects in the past at Fort Getty and has good knowledge of the land and understands the site conditions and different uses that occur presently on the site,” he wrote. “We also have a general understanding of the user groups and programming challenges, and issues to be addressed through this effort. … We anticipate that in the near term Fort Getty will continue to host both RV and tent site camping, with the expectation that this planning work be developed in a fashion that provides for a cohesive park landscape design, with refinement to the space allocated, configuration and density of the various desired uses, with provisions for the phasing of future improvements. We understand the work of the Fort Getty committee will serve to shape and guide the park programming and uses, providing direction for the development of the concept plan leading to the preferred schematic design.”
The duration of the project is anticipated to take six months. Cost estimates are not part of the scope. The project area extends from Battery Tousard north to the boat ramp, and work at this time does not include planning considerations or design related to the extant marine facilities.
“Fort Getty is a unique and highly utilized facility during the summer months with diverse user groups and a range of programming needs,” Collins wrote. “A range of improvements could expand park offerings and enhance use during the offseason for visitors and residents alike. We look forward to working with the town on the development of a schematic plan for Fort Getty.”
